source.publication: 2025 Publication OR-17, Oregon Individual Income Tax Guide
source.section: Pub OR-17 PDF p.82 'Railroad Retirement Board benefits' (subtraction code 330); Pub OR-17 PDF p.106-107 'Retirement income' (credit code 811) worksheet lines 1-12; Form OR-40 lines 7-19, 20, 24-25, 27-29 (PDF p.3-4); instructions PDF p.16 line 17 and Table 5, PDF p.16-17 line 20 and tax tables, PDF p.32 Chart S and Chart J, PDF p.17-18 line 25 and Exemption credit worksheet; Pub OR-17 PDF p.143 marginal rates

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 12,000.00 + private pension (person 0) 6,000.00 + railroad retirement (Tier 2) annuity (person 0) 2,000.00 = 20,000.00. Federal taxable income = 20,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 4,250.00 (the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form OR-40 (filing status single): line 7 federal AGI 20,000.00. Line 8 additions (Schedule OR-ASC line A5): other-state bond interest, code 158, 0.00. Line 9 = 20,000.00 + 0.00 = 20,000.00. Line 10 federal tax liability subtraction: the projection leaves it out (not_modelled), 0.00 here; the return subtracts the smaller of the federal tax and the Table 4 maximum, up to 8,500 (4,250 separate). Line 11 Social Security in federal AGI 0.00. Line 12 Oregon refund 0.00. Line 13 Schedule OR-ASC line B7: railroad retirement, code 330, 2,000.00. Line 14 = 0.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 + 2,000.00 = 2,000.00. Line 15 = 20,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 18,000.00. Line 16 itemized 0.00. Line 17 standard deduction 2,835.00; no age 65 box. Line 18 = 2,835.00. Line 19 = 18,000.00 - 2,835.00 = 15,165.00. Line 20: 4,400.00 x 4.75% = 209 + 6,700.00 x 6.75% = 452.25 + 4,065.00 x 8.75% = 355.6875; total 1016.9375, to the cent 1,016.94 (the tax table's S column, row 15,100 to 15,200, gives 1,015; expected keeps the formula). Lines 21-23 0.00. Line 24 = 1,016.94. Line 25 exemption credit: federal AGI 20,000.00 is not more than 100,000.00; 1 x 256.00 = 256.00. Line 27 retirement income credit (code 811) worksheet: line 1 and line 3 retirement income of the eligible individual(s) 6,000.00; line 2 federal pension subtracted 0.00; line 4 7,500.00; line 5 Social Security and railroad 2,000.00; line 6 = 5,500.00; line 7 household income = 20,000.00 - 0.00 + 0.00 = 20,000.00; line 8 15,000.00; line 9 = 5,000.00; line 10 = 5,500.00 - 5,000.00 = 500.00, not below 0; line 11 smaller of 6,000.00 and 500.00 = 500.00; line 12 = 500.00 x 9% = 45.00. Line 28 credits = 256.00 + 45.00 = 301.00. Line 29 and line 31 state income tax = 1,016.94 - 301.00 = 715.94. Line 32 kicker comes after this figure and is not applied (not_modelled). The railroad amount is subtracted on line 13, reduces the limit on worksheet line 5 and stays in the projection's household income measure.
accepted_approximations: The federal tax liability subtraction is not applied (not_modelled). This is the largest gap for most Oregon households.

cap_reduced_by uses all railroad_retirement income; the worksheet reduces the limit by Tier 1 benefits only. Annuity income is treated as an employee annuity plan; the credit's list names no other kind.
Tax is figured on the exact income; under 50,000 of taxable income the booklet taxes each table row at its middle and rounds, and the Department rounds at each bracket edge.
